events.title: Diamond Sutra is printed in Tang China
events.description: A block-printed copy of the Diamond Sutra was made on this date, according to its colophon. Found in a cave at Dunhuang, it is the oldest dated printed book known.
events.html: A block-printed copy of the Diamond Sutra was made on this date, according to its colophon. Found in a cave at Dunhuang, it is the oldest dated printed book known.

events.title: Columbus sails from Cádiz on his fourth voyage
events.description: Christopher Columbus set out on his last voyage, exploring the coast of Central America from Honduras to Panama. Shipwrecked on Jamaica for a year, he returned to Spain in 1504.
events.html: Christopher Columbus set out on his last voyage, exploring the coast of Central America from Honduras to Panama. Shipwrecked on Jamaica for a year, he returned to Spain in 1504.

events.title: Marshal Saxe defeats the allied army at Fontenoy
events.description: French forces under Maurice de Saxe beat British, Dutch and Hanoverian troops led by the Duke of Cumberland. The victory opened the way to the French conquest of the Austrian Netherlands.
events.html: French forces under Maurice de Saxe beat British, Dutch and Hanoverian troops led by the Duke of Cumberland. The victory opened the way to the French conquest of the Austrian Netherlands.

events.title: Prime Minister Spencer Perceval is shot in the Commons lobby
events.description: John Bellingham, a merchant with a grievance against the government, shot Perceval dead. He remains the only British prime minister to be assassinated.
events.html: John Bellingham, a merchant with a grievance against the government, shot Perceval dead. He remains the only British prime minister to be assassinated.

events.title: Mutinous sepoys from Meerut seize Delhi
events.description: Rebel soldiers rode into Delhi and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah II their leader. The Indian Rebellion that spread from here led to the end of East India Company rule in 1858.
events.html: Rebel soldiers rode into Delhi and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah II their leader. The Indian Rebellion that spread from here led to the end of East India Company rule in 1858.

events.title: India conducts nuclear tests at Pokhran
events.description: India detonated three nuclear devices in the Rajasthan desert, followed by two more on 13 May, and declared itself a nuclear weapons state. Pakistan responded with its own tests within weeks.
